title: Light traffic seen on NLEX, SLEX; almost 40K passengers at PITX on morning of Nov. 1
summary: Light traffic was seen on the North Luzon Expressway and the South Luzon Expressway on Sunday morning, November 1, as Filipinos visited the tombs of their departed loved ones in cemeteries on All…

blocks.text: Light traffic was seen on the North Luzon Expressway and the South Luzon Expressway on Sunday morning, November 1, as Filipinos visited the tombs of their departed loved ones in cemeteries on All Saints' Day (Undas).
As of 10 a.m., here's the situation on NLEX:
• Balintawak Toll Plaza - Light• Mindanao Toll Plaza - Light• Bocaue Toll Plaza - Light• San Simon Northbound - Light• San Simon Southbound - Light• San Fernando Northbound-Light
NLEX said that there is also light traffic in all other areas of NLEX-SCTEX- NLEX Connector including toll plazas and interchanges.
Meanwhile, light traffic was also observed on SLEX lanes as of 10 a.m. on Sunday morning. This includes the Magallanes/Makati to Alabang route and the Alabang to Santo Tomas route.
SKYWAY AT-GRADE/ELEVATED NB/SB Traffic Update as of 10:00 AM: Magallanes/Makati - Alabang: Light.— SLEX - MaTES (@OfficialSLEX) November 1, 2026
The overall foot traffic at the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX) meanwhile has reached 39,229 as of 8 a.m. Sunday.
PITX is expecting around 1.9 million passengers this year amid the exodus for this year's Undas break.

Several passengers have started traveling to the provinces more than a week ahead of Undas, filling bus terminals early either to beat the holiday rush or to secure their tickets before the surge of crowds.

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority already announced that the implementation of the number coding scheme will be suspended on All Souls Day on Monday, November 2. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/KG, GMA News
